correctness.rationale: Every point of the torus belongs to one of 16 affine tent/wrap cells per iterate, including boundaries; all 4096 three-step itineraries are exhaustively checked using exact Fraction algebra. The eight possible total return traces (-98,-82,-34,-2,22,38,102,198) exclude 2, so no affine fixed-equation is singular and no continuum can be lost. There are exactly 177 admissible incidences representing 100 distinct fixed \(H^3\) points, of which four are fixed H points. Direct exact evaluation yields 32 primitive cycles; all are regular and their determinant-one monodromies have traces 102 on 16 cycles, -34 on eight and -98 on eight. The checker independently compares the 32 rational canonical representatives with cycles.csv, and verifies the 18/50-grid cover and counts. These checks establish an exhaustive finite classification, not a sample. The mesh denominators follow algebraically because every return matrix is congruent to the identity modulo two and the adjugate of its fixed-point matrix is even, so the denominator divides half the absolute return determinant.

value.rationale: The symmetric two-tent cusp is a natural nonuniformly hyperbolic, polynomially mixing reference map with four known neutral period-two line families and a recently established 80-orbit period-four census. Determining its first nontrivial odd period is a motivated exact structural classification; the absence of switching three-cycles, the complete three-return Floquet spectrum, and the 18/50-grid arithmetic structure are not consequences of ergodicity or the known even-period counts. A full finite exact census has independent mathematical use as a baseline for periodic-orbit growth and for comparing smooth hyperbolic and nonsmooth/neutral short orbits; no higher-period theorem is asserted.
